question:
Select the most appropriate option to improve the bold part of the sentence.

He behaves as if he **knows everything.**
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence uses the phrase "as if he knows everything." However, the phrase "as if" typically sets up a hypothetical or unreal situation, which requires the use of the past tense.
 
• In this context, "knew everything" is the appropriate choice, as it aligns with the subjunctive mood commonly used after "as if."
 
• The use of "knows everything" in the original sentence is incorrect because it suggests certainty, which contradicts the hypothetical nature of the statement.
 
• Thus, "knew everything" is the grammatically and contextually correct option.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"He behaves as if he knew everything."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "known everything" is incorrect because "known" is the past participle form and requires an auxiliary verb (e.g., "has known").
 
• **Option 3:** "has known everything" is incorrect because it indicates present perfect tense, which does not fit the hypothetical context introduced by "as if."
 
• **Option 4:** "have known all" is incorrect because it is ungrammatical and does not fit the structure of the sentence.
